html:
1. Understanding Delaware’s Personal Care Market

Personal care agencies in Delaware provide non-medical assistance with activities of daily living, including bathing, dressing, meal preparation, and light housekeeping. Operating under the Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS), this market segment serves elderly individuals, people with disabilities, and others needing in-home support without skilled nursing care.

Key Market Indicators:

  • Growing demand driven by aging population and preference for home-based care
  • Medicaid HCBS waiver programs support in-home personal care services
  • Rural areas in Sussex and Kent counties have significant unmet demand
  • Personal Assistance Services Agency (PASA) rates average approximately $27.42/hour

2. Licensing Requirements

Personal care agencies must obtain licensure through the DHSS Division of Health Care Quality.

Application Process:

  • Submit licensing application to DHSS
  • Background checks for all staff and owners
  • Policies and procedures manual
  • Training program documentation
  • Insurance verification
  • Facility/office inspection

Ongoing Requirements:

  • Regular compliance inspections
  • Staff training documentation
  • Incident reporting
  • Quality assurance program maintenance

3. Business Structure and Registration

Required Steps:

  • Register with Delaware Division of Corporations (LLC or Corporation)
  • Obtain Delaware business license
  • Apply for federal EIN
  • Register for state tax accounts
  • Enroll as Medicaid provider (if serving Medicaid clients)

Insurance Requirements:

  • General liability insurance
  • Professional liability coverage
  • Workers’ compensation insurance
  • Bonding (recommended)
  • Vehicle insurance for staff travel

4. Financial Planning

Revenue Sources:

  • Medicaid HCBS waiver reimbursement
  • Private pay clients
  • Long-term care insurance
  • Veterans Administration programs

Financial Projections:

  • Agencies at 70-80% capacity: 15-25% gross margins
  • Break-even timeline: 12-18 months
  • Startup costs: $25,000 – $100,000

Startup Cost Breakdown:

  • Office setup: $5,000 – $20,000
  • Licensing and fees: $2,000 – $8,000
  • Insurance: $5,000 – $15,000
  • Initial marketing: $5,000 – $15,000
  • Working capital (3 months): $10,000 – $50,000

5. Service Offerings

Core Services:

  • Personal hygiene assistance (bathing, grooming, dressing)
  • Meal preparation and feeding assistance
  • Light housekeeping and laundry
  • Medication reminders (non-medical)
  • Companionship and socialization
  • Transportation to appointments
  • Errands and shopping assistance

Specialized Services:

  • Alzheimer’s and dementia companion care
  • Respite care for family caregivers
  • Post-hospitalization transition support
  • Chronic condition daily living support

6. Staffing and Training

Key Positions:

  • Agency Director/Administrator
  • Care Coordinators
  • Personal Care Aides/Attendants
  • Scheduling Staff
  • Office Administrator

Training Requirements:

  • State-approved personal care aide training
  • CPR and First Aid certification
  • Client rights and confidentiality
  • Infection control procedures
  • Emergency response protocols
  • Ongoing in-service education

7. Marketing and Growth

Client Acquisition Strategies:

  • Hospital and rehabilitation center referral partnerships
  • Physician and social worker relationship building
  • Community outreach and senior center events
  • Online presence and local SEO
  • Medicaid managed care organization contracts

Growth Opportunities:

  • Expand into underserved rural areas
  • Add specialized dementia care programs
  • Develop veteran-focused services
  • Partner with assisted living facilities for overflow care

8. Regulatory Contacts

  • DHSS Division of Health Care Quality: Primary licensing authority
  • Division of Medicaid and Medical Assistance: HCBS waiver enrollment
  • Delaware Division of Corporations: Business registration
  • Delaware Department of Labor: Employment regulations
